# ForeKingHell — complete component implementation prompts

This is an audit and implementation handoff, not a deployed redesign. The repository snapshot contains 98 page.tsx route entries: 92 rendering/guarded entries and six redirect-only entries. The pack contains 478 route-specific functional components plus 14 shared components, each with separate desktop and mobile prompts (984 viewport-specific prompts). A functional component means a user-facing section, form, table, chart, drawer or control group; its child labels/inputs/buttons are included in that prompt. Shared primitives and route boundaries are explicitly covered by G01–G14 and inherited in the route matrix.

Evidence: authenticated live inspection of the available account; 84 route patterns have a captured live/guarded/wide-runtime state, and 85 application screenshot states are retained in the evidence archive. The route-import inventory reaches 422 JSX modules; shell, CSS, capability and error-boundary source was also reviewed. The browser viewport was 1363×936. Most captures show the initial visible state rather than every scroll position or tab. The full Progress capture and selected detail pages were also inspected.

Mobile scope: companion/workbench source branches, route capabilities and the actual surface switch were reviewed. A blank wide companion view was reproduced and traced to display:none on an lg:hidden ancestor. The available browser did not expose viewport/device resizing, so no narrow-screen iPhone/Android visual pass is claimed. The prompts explicitly require 390×844, 360×800 and breakpoint verification. Physical Safari/PWA installation, offline network replay, performance benchmarks and a complete assistive-technology pass remain implementation QA tasks.

No production code was changed or deployed. No new upload, social message/invitation, shared report/link, payment, entitlement, deletion or account reset was submitted. Token-specific sharing/invitation success paths and mutation outcomes were source-reviewed and must be exercised with authorised fixtures. Guarded /import/result without an identifier is not counted as a broken successful import.

The checked-out source is main at cf9de4018e0273a7f86a0ae69791af4ff414d29c. The deployed build SHA was not independently established, so source findings and live findings are labelled separately. Current branding in the repository/site is LM World Tour; ForeKingHell is the repository/account identity. No rename is proposed.

## How to use

1. Start with the audit findings and the master contract. Implement G01, G05, G06 and G10 first, then the remaining shared components.
2. Fix the P1 Progress and Import components, then work through one complete route at a time. Implement both viewport prompts for every component on that route.
3. Copy a whole page pack or an individual component from the searchable HTML. “Include master contract” is enabled by default, so pasted instructions retain the non-negotiable constraints.
4. Use the CSV tracker to record desktop/mobile implementation and evidence separately. A page is complete only when its own components, applicable shared components, state boundaries and destination/redirect checks pass.
5. Treat proposed improvements as implementation specifications, not as proof that every current control is broken. Keep real golf renderers and business logic; change the surrounding UI and fix the specific confirmed defects.
6. Do not bulk-paste all 984 prompts into one coding turn. Complete a route-sized batch, review its screenshots and changed files, then continue with the next route. Record blocked IDs explicitly rather than silently skipping them.

## Master implementation contract

```text
Work in the existing DavidCapener182/ForeKingHell repository. This audit is grounded in commit cf9de4018e0273a7f86a0ae69791af4ff414d29c; inspect the current branch before editing and reconcile any later changes. Read AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md and the installed Next.js documentation before implementation. Keep the actual LM World Tour branding and golf identity unless David explicitly requests a rename.

Implement the selected component prompt completely for both desktop and mobile. Untitled UI is the component source and interaction reference, not a reason to replace the application with a demo. Use the exact official reference links in the prompt; inspect current exports before importing. The existing stack is Next.js 16.3, React 19, Tailwind 4, Radix/shadcn and Recharts. Introduce Untitled UI/React Aria through a clearly namespaced adapter layer. Do not run a new-project initializer or assume Radix asChild/value/onValueChange props work on React Aria components. Prefer the matching free component; if an advanced example requires a licence, record that exact blocker and implement a clearly identified composition of available base components. Do not claim a paid example was installed if it was not.

Follow the repository's full-width layout rule: do not introduce max-w-6xl, max-w-7xl or a capped dashboard/PageShell wrapper. Use the existing neutral paper surfaces, deep green accents and shared semantic tokens. Resolve duplicate font/token overrides centrally before polishing pages. Keep app typography compact and consistent; retain specialist golf diagrams, maps, course artwork and Three.js renderers. Do not add decorative heroes, unrelated stock imagery, fake dashboards, fake statistics or generic four-card rows.

Keep saved data, account scoping, permission checks, routes, units, source labels, confidence, exclusion rules, server actions and golf calculations intact. Preserve the distinction between carry and total, no-ball and with-ball speed, measured and estimated shots, real and simulator rounds, and historical and projected values. On /bag benchmark comparisons do not add Attack or Launch columns/tabs; the repository explicitly excludes them pending reliable comparison data.

Mobile is a functional delivery requirement. Inspect app-surface-server.ts, app-route-capabilities.ts, PrivateAppShell and the paired companion/workbench components. Provide the specified mobile task before removing its desktop-only handoff. Use one mutually exclusive rendering strategy at the lg boundary, and ensure an explicit companion preference cannot produce a blank main area on a wide screen. Preserve query parameters, selected entities and unsaved drafts across surface changes. Use CSS layout breakpoints for layout, not user-agent assumptions alone.

Verify each selected component at 1440x900 and 1280x800, at 390x844 and 360x800, and at 1023/1024px around the shared breakpoint. Check keyboard use, visible focus, screen-reader names, 200% zoom, long names, empty data, loading, error, partial data and the component-specific acceptance criteria. Do not hide a failing component to pass screenshots. For stateful changes add only meaningful regression checks: query persistence, arithmetic, permissions, mutations or draft recovery as relevant. Reuse the project's existing test commands. Use authorised fixtures for uploads, destructive actions, payments, invitations and sharing; do not exercise those against live personal data simply to prove the UI.

Return the completed component IDs, exact changed files, desktop and mobile screenshots at the requested sizes, verification results and concrete blockers. Keep an explicit list of incomplete IDs; do not mark a page complete while a prompt on it remains unimplemented. Do not deploy or claim this audit itself changed production.
```
